summary.name: Sikemux
summary.one_liner: Sikemux is a free, MIT-licensed native desktop workspace that runs Claude Code, Codex and other coding agents side by side on your own subscriptions, with terminals, Git, an editor and browser tabs beside each chat.
keywords: terminal and git in one window
run agents on my own subscription
use_cases: Running several coding agents on one project at once
Continuing a chat with another agent when one plan's usage runs out
Reviewing which agent wrote each change before committing
Having agents test a web app in a built-in browser tab
Getting permission prompts from agents on a phone or the MacBook notch
Working with issues, pull requests and CI without leaving the app
summary.what_it_does: Sikemux is a desktop app where you run AI coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex in a single window. You install an agent the usual way and sign in; Sikemux detects it and starts it with your own login, and does not provide a model of its own. Agents read the project, edit files and run commands while you watch, and the app shows which agent is working, waiting on you, or done. Each agent gets terminals, Git, an editor and a browser tab next to its chat, and agents can message each other and hand off work. The page also describes alerts on the MacBook notch and an iPhone app for answering agent prompts.
notable: Native app drawn on the GPU rather than Electron; whole download listed at 32.0 MB
Lets a chat continue with another agent when one plan's usage runs out
Notch island and iPhone app to answer agent permission requests
Agents can message each other and hand off work; Chief agent coordinates per project
caveats: Intel Macs have no download yet; they can build from source
Linux app requires Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13 or newer for the full app; older systems need the core-only install
Android app is listed as in testing
Page says future paid offerings may appear for hosted agents, sync and team features; the app itself is stated to stay free
